newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission says to answer any mad cow charges.
newsitem.headline: Commission says to answer any mad cow charges.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer will answer any criticism made of the Commission in the European Parliament's final report on mad cow disease, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said on Wednesday.

Internal reorganisation of the Commission's agriculture department (DGVI) will go ahead and should be completed before Santer addresses the parliament in Strasbourg on February 19 to answer all charges, he added.

He angrily denied a report that the Commission had concealed minutes of its meetings from the Parliament's temporary committee of inquiry, which Belgium's French-language newspaper Le Soir reported on Tuesday.

Van der Pas said extracts of a leaked document had been taken out of context and added that if others had been quoted they would have shown that the Commission had taken a consistent line on the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopthy (BSE) crisis, he told a news briefing.
"The Commission will continue that constant line and will call on all those who have been party to this discussion to come down to earth," he said.
He denied that the Commission had favoured the British government during developments in the crisis involving the brain-wasting disease linked to the human equivalent Creutzfeld Jacob Disease (CJD).
His remarks concerned doubts surrounding how well Britain policed a ban on suspect animal feed made from meat and bone meal after it was introduced in 1989.
The Commission imposed a world-wide ban on British beef exports in March last year after a government statement in Britain's House of Commons saying BSE could be linked to CJD.
The draft report from the European Parliament's temporary committee of inquiry into BSE has criticised both the Commission and the British government.
"The Commission will take a position on each point in the final report when it is available," van der Pas added.
